parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator any thermal runaway, fire, explosion, injury, evacuation, or material property damage involving a unit within 24 hours of learning of it, followed by a preliminary investigation report within 10 business days and a final report within 30 days or when the investigation concludes. Suspected thermal incidents without injury or damage must be reported within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly, and no later than 5 business days after determining that a safety notice or action is warranted.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator any thermal runaway, fire, explosion, injury, evacuation, or material property damage involving a unit within 24 hours of learning of it, followed by a preliminary investigation report within 10 business days and a final report within 30 days or when the investigation concludes. S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator any thermal runaway, fire, explosion, injury, evacuation, or material property damage involving a unit within 24 hours of learning of it, followed by a preliminary investigation report within 10 business days and a final report within 30 days or when the investigation concludes. Suspected thermal incidents without injury or damage must be reported within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly, and no later than 5 business days after determining that a safety notice or action is warranted. Reports must include model, serial number, location, and known circumstances, subject to applicable privacy protections.

parameters.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative units. Results and test methods must be provided to current owners and prospective customers before purchase; individual-unit identifying information may be withheld. A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly notify the regulator and submit a corrective-action plan with milestones. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale or require withdrawal of existing units; restrictions must be based on an individualized safety assessment and proportionate corrective action.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative units. Results and test methods must be provided to current owners and prospective customers before purchase; individual-unit identifying information may be withheld. A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly notify the regulator and submit a corrective-action plan with milestones. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale or require withdrawal of existing units; restrictions must be based on an individualized safety assessment and proportionate corrective action.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative units. Before market entry and at least annually thereafter, manufacturers must test and submit per-model results and supporting methods to the regulator. Results and test methods must be provided to current owners and prospective customers before purchase; individual-unit identifying information may be withheld. A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly notify the regulator and submit a corrective-action plan with milestones. The regulator may require further testing or risk controls based on the evidence. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale or require withdrawal of existing units; restrictions must be based on an individualized safety assessment and proportionate corrective action.

parameters.quote: All newly installed systems must include a remotely operable emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a locally accessible shut-off as backup. Existing installed units must be brought into compliance or replaced within 6 years of this standard taking effect; where retrofit is technically infeasible, the manufacturer must provide an equivalent safety measure approved by the regulator.

S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: All newly installed systems must include a remotely operable emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a locally accessible shut-off as backup. Manufacturers must provide owners clear instructions and test the function during commissioning. Existing installed units must be brought into compliance or replaced within 6 years of this standard taking effect; where retrofit is technically infeasible, the manufacturer must provide an equivalent safety measure approved by the regulator.

parameters.quote: New home battery systems must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard takes effect. The suppression system must be suitable for the battery chemistry and installation, and must be tested under a regulator-approved protocol.

S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New home battery systems must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers must provide owners with maintenance and inspection instructions.

parameters.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a mandatory recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period. The manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers promptly, explain the risk and remedy, and provide the remedy at no cost.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A manufacturer must initiate a mandatory recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period. The manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers promptly, explain the risk and remedy, and provide the remedy at no cost.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers, before purchase and throughout ownership, clear safety notices describing material hazards, required precautions, emergency response and shut-off instructions, and any applicable corrective actions. Notices must be delivered promptly in accessible formats and languages appropriate to the customer base. A manufacturer must initiate a mandatory recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period. The manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers promptly, explain the risk and remedy, and provide the remedy at no cost. Regulators may require additional action where the risk warrants it.

judge_section_notes: S1 imposes strict reporting: serious incidents within 24 hours, other suspected incidents within 10 business days, and customer notice within 5 business days. S2 keeps a 55 °C test and 5% threshold but removes any automatic sales ban, instead requiring corrective-action plans and customer/regulator access to results, not public disclosure. S3 requires new-unit shut-off immediately and a 6-year retrofit deadline with an infeasibility alternative; S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months; S5 mandates recall at 8 incidents/100k with prompt notices but no explicit serious-injury clause.
